name: For teachers
title: For teachers — Geek Informatic
description: How to use Geek Informatic in a lesson: free, no sign-up, a list of activities by grade and direct links to levels, rebuses and mazes.
ogDescription: A practical guide for teachers: activities by grade, direct links for students and lesson tips.
lead: A short guide to using the site in a lesson: what is on it, how to give students an exact link and what to do about shared computers.
how.1: Free and with no sign-up: students simply open a link.
how.2: Works in any modern browser on a computer or tablet.
how.3: Progress is saved in the browser on that device.
how.4: The site doesn’t collect student data; see the [“Privacy”](@privacy/) page for details.
how.5: The site comes in Ukrainian and English: there is a language switch in the header of every page. “Drive the Robot!”, “Galaxy Code”, “Mars Rover Maze” and “Cyber Shield Agents” are available in English; the rebuses are Ukrainian only for now. Progress in the games is shared between the two languages.

act.name: Title
do.agenty-kibershchytu: Complete {count.agenty-kibershchytu} {count.agenty-kibershchytu|mission|missions} about passwords, phishing and fakes, collect key letters and receive an agent ID card.
do.kod-galaktyky: Build a block program (moves, turns, repeats) for the droid to collect crystals across {count.kod-galaktyky} {count.kod-galaktyky|level|levels}.
do.robot: Build a program from arrows and “Repeat” blocks so the robot collects every crystal across {count.robot} {count.robot|level|levels}.
do.mars: Assemble the right-hand rule from blocks and test it on new mazes.
do.rebusy: Solve rebuses made of pictures, commas and swapped letters and find computer terms.
act.filter: You can also filter activities on the [home page](@).
links.lead: To get the whole class onto the same task at once, give students a ready-made link. Every example below can be copied as is.
links.robot: **Robot:** `#level-name` opens that level even if the earlier ones aren’t finished. For example, level 6 (“Loop magic”): `https://otianoleksij.github.io/geek-informatic/en/games/robot/#loop-magic`. Level names: `first-step`, `turn`, `around-rocks`, `tricky-path`, `stone-corridor`, `loop-magic`, `staircase`, `loop-combo`, `maze`, `crystal-mountain`. Old number-based links (`#level-6`) still work.
links.galaxy: **Galaxy Code:** `#level-name` opens that level even if the earlier ones aren’t finished. For example, level 10 (“Perimeter”): `https://otianoleksij.github.io/geek-informatic/en/games/kod-galaktyky/#perimeter`. Level names: `first-crystal`, `left-and-right`, `asteroid-maze`, `long-road`, `ladder`, `around-the-rock`, `every-other-cell`, `no-right-turn`, `tight-hangar`, `perimeter`, `zigzag`, `pinwheel`, `two-rings`, `grid`, `station-heart`. Number-based links (`#level-10`) also work.
links.mars: **Mars Rover:** `#maze-number` gives the whole class the same maze: `https://otianoleksij.github.io/geek-informatic/en/games/mars/#maze-12345`. The number appears in the address bar after you press “New maze”.
links.kiber: **Cyber Shield Agents:** there are no direct links to missions; they open in order.
links.catalog: **Catalog on the home page:** `?grade=7` shows activities for grade 7: `https://otianoleksij.github.io/geek-informatic/en/?grade=7`. `type`, `topic` and `level` (difficulty 1–3) work too.
tips.1: **Shared computers.** At the end of the lesson, ask students to clear their data on the [“Privacy”](@privacy/) page so the next class starts from scratch.
tips.2: **CyberShield ID card.** The name and grade aren’t saved, so students enter them while the page is open. The ID card can be shown on screen, captured in a screenshot, or the result line can be copied and sent to the teacher.
tips.3: **Keyboard.** The block editors (Galaxy Code, Mars Rover) have a “Keyboard controls” help section for students who find the mouse awkward.
tips.4: **Same conditions for everyone.** Share one class-wide link to a level or a maze so that solutions can be compared.
